entities.label: The FFRDC Seam
entities.sub: Structural domain - the legal space between government and industry
entities.desc: This is the mechanism the whole board turns on, and it is not a theory - it is written into the Federal Acquisition Regulation. A federally funded research and development center is a research organisation operated under contract by a private entity - a nonprofit, a university, or an industrial consortium - to meet a special long-term research need that, in the FAR's language, cannot be met as effectively by existing in-house or contractor resources. As of February 2026 there were 41 FFRDCs sponsored or co-sponsored by 12 federal agencies. Three features of FAR 35.017 create the seam. First, sponsors are directed to build long-term strategic relationships: initial contracts may run five years and are renewable in similar increments, expressly to give the FFRDC stability, continuity and the ability to attract high-quality personnel. Second, and decisively, the FFRDC 'has access to government and supplier data, including sensitive and proprietary information, and to employees and facilities beyond that common in a normal contractual relationship.' That single clause creates an entity that can legally see both the government's compartmented information and the prime contractor's proprietary information - a vantage no ordinary contractor and no ordinary civil servant has. Third, in exchange for that access, the FFRDC is barred from competing with the private sector for federal R&D work and is required to operate in the public interest with objectivity, free from organisational conflicts of interest, and to fully disclose its activities to its sponsoring agency - to the sponsor, note, not to Congress and not to the public. The consequence is the concealment architecture in miniature. Records held by an FFRDC are contractor records, not agency records, and therefore outside the Freedom of Information Act. Disclosure runs to the sponsoring agency, which is also the classification authority. Sole-source awards mean no competitor ever audits the work. Personnel move continuously between the sponsor and the operator. If a programme wanted to be technically vested outside the government while the government retained absolute control of materials, breakthroughs and data - and while remaining invisible to FOIA, to GAO, and to committee staff without the sponsor's consent - it would be built exactly here. Rep. Eric Burlison made this the explicit basis of his May 2026 inquiry: FFRDCs, he wrote, 'often receive special access to government facilities, data, sponsor requirements, and sensitive technical information that ordinary private contractors may not receive,' and 'cannot become private vaults for federal records.'

entities.label: FAR 35.017 - Federally Funded Research and Development Centers
entities.sub: Federal Acquisition Regulation subpart; 48 CFR 35.017
entities.desc: The regulatory instrument that creates the seam. FAR 35.017 defines what an FFRDC is, requires a sponsoring agency to justify its existence, sets the terms of the sponsoring agreement, and grants the operator its extraordinary access. The operative language for this board is the access clause - an FFRDC 'has access to government and supplier data, including sensitive and proprietary information, and to employees and facilities beyond that common in a normal contractual relationship' - and the disclosure clause, which requires the FFRDC to fully disclose its activities to its sponsoring agency. Nothing in FAR 35.017 requires disclosure to Congress, to the public, to GAO, or to any other agency. The sponsor is simultaneously the customer, the classification authority, and the only body entitled to a full account of what the FFRDC does. Contracts may be awarded for up to five years and renewed indefinitely in like increments, and are routinely awarded sole-source: the government's own notices for MITRE's aviation FFRDC in 2025 were posted as notices of intent to award a sole source contract. In return the FFRDC is forbidden to compete for federal R&D work against industry and must operate free of organisational conflicts of interest. Read as a whole, the subpart constructs an entity with the government's access, the private sector's records status, and no independent auditor. It is the legal chassis on which every entity in this domain sits.

entities.desc: MITRE is the priority institution of this domain and, on the board's premise, the structural heart of the concealment architecture. It was created by the Air Force, explicitly on the RAND model, to be a permanent nonprofit answerable to a military customer rather than to a university. It now operates six FFRDCs: the National Security Engineering Center for the Department of Defense under the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering; the Center for Advanced Aviation System Development for the FAA; the Center for Enterprise Modernization for Treasury and IRS with VA, SSA and Commerce as co-sponsors; the Homeland Security Systems Engineering and Development Institute for DHS S&T, created 5 March 2009; the Health FFRDC for HHS; and the National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence for NIST, created 19 September 2014. entities.desc: Los Alamos National Laboratory, administered by Triad National Security, LLC, sits on the Pajarito Plateau in northern New Mexico. It was the site of the 16 February 1949 conference on green fireballs attended by Norris Bradbury, Edward Teller and Frederick Reines with FBI, AEC and military representatives, whose minutes the laboratory's National Security Research Center still holds. Together with Sandia and Kirtland to the south, it forms the New Mexico nuclear triangle over which the 1948-51 green fireball flap was concentrated - and which is the geographic centre of nearly every legacy-programme allegation from Roswell forward.

d-ffrdc.desc: How the seam actually works, mechanism by mechanism. (1) RECORDS STATUS. Documents created and held by an FFRDC operator are the contractor's records, not agency records. The Freedom of Information Act reaches agency records. A congressional committee can subpoena a contractor, but it must first know the contractor holds something - which is why Burlison's method of naming a file by its exact designation, as he did with AF-ATIC-FILM 03/52 at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, worked where a general request would not have. (2) DISCLOSURE DIRECTION. FAR 35.017 obliges the FFRDC to fully disclose its activities to its sponsoring agency. The sponsor is simultaneously the customer, the funder and the original classification authority. There is no obligation running to Congress, to GAO, to the public, or to any other agency. MITRE's answer to Burlison - that it would 'coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work' - is not evasion in the colloquial sense; it is the regulation operating exactly as written. (3) DUAL ACCESS. The FFRDC sees the government's compartmented information and the prime contractor's proprietary information. No civil servant has the second; no ordinary contractor has the first. That is the informational chokepoint the 2026 UAP Gerb investigation identifies as the 'missing link', and it exists whether or not any of that investigation's specific allegations are true. (4) NON-COMPETITION. Because the FFRDC is barred from competing with industry for federal R&D, no commercial rival ever has cause or standing to audit its work. (5) PERPETUITY. Five-year contracts renewable indefinitely, awarded sole-source, produce institutional relationships measured in decades - MITRE's DoD relationship is 68 years old, Battelle's Pacific Northwest contract dates to 1978, UT-Battelle's Oak Ridge contract runs to 2030. (6) PERSONNEL FLOW. The same executives move between sponsor and operator: a former NRO director chairs MITRE's board, a former PDDNI is its vice chair, a Battelle executive is its CEO, a former STRATCOM commander runs IDA, a former IARPA director runs RAND, and AARO's founding director went to Oak Ridge. Put these six together and you have an entity with the government's access, the private sector's records status, no auditor, no expiry and a shared talent pool with its own overseer. The board's position is not that this proves a concealed programme exists. It is that if one exists, this is where it lives, and that the burden of demonstrating otherwise sits with the institutions that built the structure.

mitre-corporation.desc: FY2024 FFRDC funding places MITRE's National Security Engineering Center at approximately $1,431.7 million, ahead of the Aerospace FFRDC ($1,309.8 million) and MIT Lincoln Laboratory ($1,360.6 million), and behind only the DOE weapons and multiprogram laboratories - Sandia ($4,584.0 million), Los Alamos ($3,918.3 million), JPL ($2,647.8 million), Livermore ($2,188.8 million), Oak Ridge ($2,091.2 million), Idaho ($1,594.1 million) and Pacific Northwest ($1,585.7 million). MITRE's total corporate revenue passed $2.37 billion in 2023. Contract vehicles documented on USAspending: NSEC through Army Contracting Command IDIQ W56KGU18D0004 with annual task orders W56KGU20F0009 ($583m), W56KGU21F0008 ($618m), W56KGU22F0017 ($687m), W56KGU23F0006 ($731m) and W56KGU24F0010 ($752m); CAASD through FAA contracts DTFAWA10C00080 ($1.70bn) and 693KA822C00001 ($761m). Governance since 2015: Rodney E. Slater, former Secretary of Transportation, as board chair; Donald Kerr, former Los Alamos director, NRO director and Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, elected chairman in November 2018 with former House Intelligence Committee chairman Mike Rogers as vice chairman; Sue Gordon, former Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, joining in 2021 and elected vice chair on 31 October 2023; Paul Kaminski, former Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Technology, retiring from the board in 2025; Samantha Ravich, former vice chair of the President's Intelligence Advisory Board, elected 19 May 2026. Executive leadership: Mark Peters (President and CEO, from Battelle), Dana Keoki Jackson (SVP and GM, MITRE National Security, from Lockheed Martin's CTO office), Charles Clancy (CTO), Greg Crawford (Deputy GM, National Security), Austin Wang (VP, Intelligence Center), Yosry Barsoum (VP, Center for Securing the Homeland), Christopher Land (General Counsel and Secretary to the Board). That last title matters procedurally: the officer who determines MITRE's legal response to a congressional production request is the same officer who serves as secretary to the board chaired and vice-chaired by former senior intelligence officials.

battelle.desc: Battelle's laboratory portfolio is the largest single concentration of contractor-operated federal research capacity in the United States, and it is the reason the institution recurs at both ends of this board's chronology. Battelle Memorial Institute is sole operator of Pacific Northwest National Laboratory under DOE contract DEAC0576RL01830, on USAspending since 1978 with obligations exceeding $30.6 billion; co-operator of Oak Ridge National Laboratory through UT-Battelle LLC under DEAC0500OR22725, approximately $42.3 billion, 1999-2030; operator of Idaho National Laboratory through Battelle Energy Alliance LLC; a partner in the National Renewable Energy Laboratory and Brookhaven National Laboratory; and operator of the National Biodefense Analysis and Countermeasures Center for DHS. In FY2024 the Battelle-affiliated laboratories alone accounted for roughly $5.27 billion in FFRDC funding (ORNL $2,091.2m, INL $1,594.1m, PNNL $1,585.7m). The UFO record: Project Stork, the Air Force analytical contract, 1952-1955; Blue Book Special Report No. 14, 5 May 1955; the Pentacle Memorandum, 9 January 1953; Wright-Patterson-sponsored nickel-titanium alloy research in 1948-49 whose reports researchers allege are missing from both Air Force and Battelle archives; the ORNL analysis of AARO's magnesium specimen, contracted 2022, reported April 2024; Sean Kirkpatrick's move to ORNL in December 2023; and Mark Peters's move from Battelle headquarters to the MITRE chief executive's office in September 2024. Each link is individually documented. The board's claim about them collectively is a tier-3 inference stated as such: that custody of the government's anomalous-materials analysis capability has stayed inside one institutional family for seventy years, not because of conspiracy but because the government has never built the capability anywhere else.

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.desc: The compliance schedule, in full, as reported by MeriTalk and DefenseScoop from the letter text: designate a senior officer responsible for the response within 5 business days; issue a litigation-style preservation hold within 10 business days; coordinate a classified briefing for cleared committee staff within 14 days; deliver written responses and a records-location index within 30 days; produce unclassified materials in native electronic format with complete metadata within 45 days; and separately identify all classified or sponsor-controlled materials with the controlling authority named. MITRE must account for records created, handled, transferred, withheld or destroyed by the corporation, by any of its six FFRDCs, or by its subcontractors. Coverage extends to UAP detection and tracking across air, space, maritime, cyber and electromagnetic domains, and to MITRE work involving Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Raytheon, Boeing, General Dynamics, SAIC and Leidos. The temporal reach - back to 1930 - is unusual and deliberate: it predates MITRE's own 1958 founding, which means the request captures predecessor and inherited holdings including anything that travelled with the 485 staff who came from MIT Lincoln Laboratory. Counting from 22 May 2026, the 45-day unclassified production deadline fell on approximately 6 July 2026 and the 30-day index deadline on approximately 21 June 2026. As of 12 August 2026 no public production, index, or classified briefing outcome has been reported, and Burlison's office has not announced non-compliance. That silence is the open item on this board.

gaps: MITRE's response to the 22 May 2026 letter is unpublished. The 30-day records index deadline fell around 21 June 2026 and the 45-day unclassified production deadline around 6 July 2026; as of 12 August 2026 no index, production, privilege log or classified-briefing outcome has been made public, and Burlison's office has not announced non-compliance. Obtaining the index - or confirmation that none was produced - is the single highest-value next step in this domain.

No letter has been made public to RAND, the Aerospace Corporation, IDA or Sandia despite Burlison naming RAND, Aerospace and MIT Lincoln Labs on the record. Confirm via the Oversight Committee whether letters were sent and not publicised, or not sent at all.

The specific UAP Gerb allegations - a MITRE reverse-engineering charter dating to 1958, the Atlantic 'tic tac factory' USO tasking, and the 2011 briefing restriction on historical programme incumbents - rest on no produced document. Identify whether the claimed 2011 restriction corresponds to any real classification guide change, DD Form 254 revision or SAP annual report notation.

The identity and standing of 'Kerberos', the researcher credited with the MITRE case in the 7 August 2026 investigation, is unestablished. Whether that person has first-hand access or is purely an open-source analyst materially changes the tier of every allegation in the piece.

MITRE's DD Form 254 contract security classification specifications for NSEC task orders under W56KGU18D0004 have not been sought. These specify exactly which compartments a contractor is accredited for and are the most direct documentary route to establishing MITRE's SAP access profile without relying on testimony.

The Battelle nickel-titanium reports of 1948-49 remain unlocated. Bragalia's allegation that they are missing from both Air Force and Battelle archives has never been tested by a formal congressional records demand to Battelle - which, unlike MITRE, has not received one.

No signed original of the Pentacle Memorandum has ever been produced by the Air Force or by Battelle; only Vallee's copy and transcription circulate. A NARA search of Wright-Patterson ATIC correspondence for reference G-1579-4 and for Miles E. Goll's files has not been publicly attempted.

University Affiliated Research Centers - JHU APL above all - are entirely outside the current inquiry despite carrying FFRDC-like access without the FAR 35.017 registration regime, and despite the Navy-centric character of the whole legacy-programme record. No congressional UAP letter has gone to a UARC.

The relationship between AARO and the FFRDC layer is undocumented beyond the ORNL materials contract. Whether AARO tasked MITRE, Aerospace, RAND or IDA for analytic support, and under what vehicles, has not been established from contract data.

Whether the FY2027 NDAA's contractor-records provision survives the Senate and conference is unresolved, and it is the only proposed mechanism that would reach inside an FFRDC without the sponsoring agency's consent. Track the conference report language specifically for the definition of 'covered records' and whether FFRDC operators are named.

The 1949 Los Alamos conference minutes held by LANL's National Security Research Center have been acknowledged but not published in full. A targeted FOIA or NARA request for the minutes themselves, rather than for 'Project Twinkle', is the obvious unexecuted step.

Aerospace Corporation's role in space-based sensor characterisation of anomalous objects is entirely uninvestigated. Its DOE nonproliferation contract 89233120CNA000134 and its Space Force FFRDC contract FA880219C0001 are the vehicles under which any such work would sit.
